fix(models): decoder-only multi-dataset training for ensemble models (#1401)

## Description

I am currently working with the new multi-dataset functionality where
encoders and decoders are configured separately. I'd like to fit a model
where the other dataset has only a decoder, but no encoder. In this
setting I think I've run into two separate issues. First is that in this
case for the decoder I'd like to have

```
decoders:
  other:
    target_datasets: [ "other" ]
    target_node_features: [ "prognostics" ] # rather than the default value encoded_data as there is no encoded data, but prognostics do exist.
```

It appears that the index in some cases is not moved to the correct
device and there is a CPU/GPU-mismatch (index is exists on the CPU
whereas the data that the index is subsetting is on the GPU).


Another missing feature I'd like to add (in a separate commit but also
in this PR) for the same training use case is related to also allowing
for no residual connections when there is no encoder.

Specifically allowing for `x_skip` to be `None` is only implemented for
`encoder_processor_decoder` but not for the ensemble version. I simply
copied the relevant parts so that this should now also work for the
ensemble version.

## What problem does this change solve?

* `target_node_features: ["prognostics"]` should now work correctly for
the aforementioned case.
* it should be possible to have `x_skip` be `None` for ensemble encoder
processor decoder -model.

## What issue or task does this change relate to?

Closes #1400, which describes the first bug in more detail.

This is my first PR to anemoi so I'll definitely accept feedback on how
you'd want the fixes! Also if there is something I've missed or tests

commit.message:
fix(training): fix compile error when using activation checkpointing (#1344)

## Description
Fixes an error when using torch compiled code inside a checkpointed
region.

the error was reported
[here](https://github.com/ecmwf/anemoi-core/issues/1330) with more
background [here](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/166926). The
fix comes from [here](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/1991)
and is only available for torch 2.10 and above. I have added a warning
if you use compilation and torch < 2.10 which lists some workarounds.
but the proper solution is upgrading torch.

It also fixes another cause of recompilation errors:
`torch._inductor.config.shape_padding` can pad tensors based on
micro-benchmarks. if you recompile inside a checkpointed reason this can
lead to shape mismatches. I disable this feature when using gradient
checkpointing. I also warn users about other settings e.g.
"mode='max-autotune'" which could lead to errors when used with gradient
checkpointing.

Lastly, I set a default number of CPU threads. Otherwise this was being
reset multiple times by PytorchLightning during runtime. Each time it
was set, it would trigger a needless recompilation, which used up one of
the 'model.recompile_limit' recompilations

I got Claude to generate a reproducer, using the compiled conditional
layer norm in anemoi (see
[here](https://github.com/ecmwf/anemoi-core/blob/3cb72df1f1767b8588b518b0c6e9af98f3e4893c/reproduce_compile_checkpoint_lru.py))
the error fires when the cache is enabled, and doesn't fire when the
cache is disabled.

docs(training): fix stale config paths in user-guide (#1391)

Correct several config-key references in the training user guide that no
longer match the current schema / shipped configs:

- tracking.rst: 'config.diagnostics.logger.mlflow.*' ->
'config.diagnostics.log.mlflow.*' (the Hydra group is 'diagnostics/log/'
  and defaults use '- log: mlflow'). Also drop the stray '.evaluation.'
  from the experiment_name path; 'experiment_name' is a direct field on
  the mlflow logger config.

- training.rst 'Data Routing': 'config.data.datasets.<name>.forcings' /
'.diagnostics' -> singular '.forcing' / '.diagnostic', matching
'DatasetDataSchema' in 'training/schemas/data.py' and the shipped
'config/data/zarr.yaml'. YAML example updated to match.

- training.rst 'Normalisation': the normaliser is not a direct field on
the dataset; it is a processor. Update the referenced path to
'config.data.datasets.<name>.processors.normalizer.config' and rewrite
the YAML examples to match the shipped 'config/data/zarr.yaml' layout,
including the '_target_' / 'config:' indirection and the American
'normalizer' spelling that the code uses.

- training.rst 'Loss Functions':
'config.training.datasets.<name>.node_weights' does not exist. Node
weighting is applied via the 'node_weights' scaler under
'config.training.scalers.<dataset_name>.node_weights'; describe that
mechanism (set 'nodes_attribute_name', reference from a loss' 'scalers:'
list) with 'area_weight' as the default.

- training.rst 'Learning rate': replace 'config.training.lr.rate /
.iterations / .min / .warmup_t' with the actual paths
'config.training.optimization.lr' and
'config.training.optimization.lr_scheduler.{t_initial,lr_min,warmup_t}',
matching 'OptimizationSchema' and
'config/training/optimization/lr_scheduler/cosine_scheduler.yaml'. Also
correct the scheduler attribution: 'CosineLRScheduler' comes from
'timm', not 'PyTorch'.

- training.rst rollout section:
'config.dataloader.training.limit_batches' ->
'config.dataloader.limit_batches.training', matching the actual nesting
in 'config/dataloader/native_grid.yaml'.

- basic-set-up.rst: update the 'Anemoi Training repository' link that
pointed at the pre-merger 'ecmwf/anemoi-training' repo to the current
monorepo location 'ecmwf/anemoi-core/tree/main/training', and update the
referenced path prefix accordingly.

commit.message:
fix(training): scale prog variable at data index 0 in the tendency scaler (#1369)

AI summary:

## Background

The tendency scalers (`stdev_tendency` and `var_tendency`) adjust how
much each
predicted variable counts towards the training loss. They do this by
comparing
how much a variable varies overall with how much it changes from one
time step to
the next. A variable that changes only slowly gets a larger weight, so
that slow
variables and fast variables both contribute meaningfully to the loss.

## The problem

When the scaler works out the weight for each variable, it first checked
whether
the variable exists in the dataset. That check was written as:

    self.data_indices.data.output.name_to_index.get(key)

This returns the position of the variable in the dataset, for example 0,
1, 2 and
so on. In Python the number 0 counts as false. So for the variable that
happens to
sit at position 0, the check failed and the variable was skipped
entirely.

A skipped variable keeps a weight of 1.0 instead of the weight the
scaler was
supposed to give it. Variables in a dataset are ordered by position, and
the
variable at position 0 is usually one of the predicted ones, so this
affected most
training configurations that use a tendency scaler.

Please note that this changes the loss weights compared with previous
runs. Runs
started before this fix used different weights, so results will not
match exactly.

## Why the check was removed instead of corrected

The check is not needed at all any more, so it has been deleted rather
than
rewritten.

It was added at a time when the model could split one dataset variable
into
several model variables. For example, a wind or wave direction was
converted into
its cosine and its sine, because an angle jumps from 359 degrees back to
0 degrees
and that is difficult to learn directly. The two new variables existed
inside the
model but not in the dataset, so they had no statistics, and the check
was there to
skip them.

That feature was removed in #268 and the conversion is now done when the
dataset is
built instead. Since then, every variable the model produces also exists
in the
dataset, so the check could never fail. Removing it avoids leaving a
test in the
code that suggests a situation that can no longer happen.

## Other changes in this pull request

- The code now checks whether tendency statistics are `None` explicitly,
rather
than relying on Python's true or false interpretation of a dictionary.
This is
  the same kind of mistake as the one described above.

- The two warning messages in the tendency scaler now go through the
normal
logger and say which scaler and which dataset they refer to. Previously
they
did not, which was confusing because the shipped configuration files
create both
tendency scalers even when the loss does not use them, so the same
anonymous
  warning could appear twice.

- The temporal downscaler configuration files now explain why the
  `output_left_boundary` option requires the tendency timestep to be set
explicitly. When that option is switched on, the first output step is 0
hours
ahead, and there is no such thing as a change over 0 hours, so no
statistics
exist for it. Without an explicit timestep the scaler picks the first
available
  lead time, finds nothing, and training stops with an error at startup.

## Tests

Three unit tests were added in `test_loss_scaling.py`:

1. Every predicted variable, including the one at position 0, receives
the weight
calculated from its own statistics. This test fails if the old check is
put
   back.
2. A dataset with no tendency statistics leaves all weights at 1.0 and
writes a
   warning naming the scaler and the dataset.
3. When no timestep is configured, the scaler falls back to the first
available
   lead time and reports this.
